admin.activityNoPageViews: Ordinary page views are not recorded. This log holds actions that changed something, requests that were refused, and access to student work — not a record of everywhere a person has been.
admin.activityRefused: {count, plural, one {# request was refused} other {# requests were refused}} in this period. A handful is ordinary — a stale link, a class someone no longer teaches. A great many from one person is worth asking about.
admin.activitySubtitle: Consequential actions in this institution, newest first.
admin.healthLongestWaitHint: someone is still waiting this long
admin.healthNeedsAttention: {count, plural, one {# course needs attention} other {# courses need attention}}
admin.healthNoSurveillanceNote: These figures are drawn from work set and marked. Scholar does not report on how individual students spend their time, and no measure of attention, engagement or study habits is available here or anywhere else in the administration console.
admin.healthSubtitle: What the institution has set, returned, and left waiting — over the last 90 days.
admin.healthTypicalWaitHint: from handing in to getting it back
admin.overviewSubtitle: How the institution is set up, and what it is doing.
admin.settingsAiHelp: Whether teachers can ask a model to suggest a mark. Doing so sends the student's submitted work to whichever provider is configured, so this is a decision about where your students' coursework goes — not a convenience setting. A suggestion never becomes a grade on its own; a teacher always records it.
admin.settingsAiInstitutionHelp: Teachers may ask for a suggestion, using the provider you configure. They cannot change it.
admin.settingsAiOffHelp: No student work is sent to any model.
admin.settingsAiTeacherHelp: Each teacher uses their own provider and key. You will not know which.
admin.settingsAiTeacherWarning: With this setting your institution cannot say where its students' work is being sent, because each teacher decides separately. If you are subject to the GDPR, the UK Age Appropriate Design Code or India's DPDP Act, that is likely to be a problem worth checking before you choose it.
admin.settingsDaysOffHelp: Which days your students are not at school. Scholar uses this to work out when they actually have time to study, so getting it wrong means telling someone to start an essay on a day they are in lessons.
admin.settingsDeadlineMeans: A deadline set for Friday 23:59 means
admin.settingsDeadlinesUnchanged: Changing the timezone does not move deadlines that already exist — each one keeps the clock it was written against, so nobody becomes late because a setting changed.
admin.settingsGradesHelp: How marks are written down for students and parents. Scholar always works out the same underlying figure from marks and weights — this decides only how it is written, so changing it re-labels existing grades rather than recalculating them.
admin.settingsLowerIsBetter: On this scale a lower number is a better result. Scholar orders and colours grades accordingly.
admin.settingsNoDaysOffWarning: With no days off, Scholar will assume your students are available every day.
admin.settingsSaved: Saved. New deadlines will use this clock.
admin.settingsTimezoneHelp: The clock your teachers write deadlines against. A student reading a deadline from another country sees their own time alongside this one, so the rule stays the rule wherever they are.

settings-rest.accountInfoBulletText: your name and email address, either entered directly or provided by the sign-in method you choose (Google or GitHub). We only ever request basic profile info and an email address — never posts, friends lists, or other social data.
settings-rest.alertsDescription: Scholar only raises these when the numbers actually warrant it — there are no recurring reminders and nothing fires on a timer.
settings-rest.appearanceDescription: Pick any accent color — it reskins buttons, gradients, focus rings and the ambient background everywhere in Scholar, and follows your account to any device you sign into.
settings-rest.changesToPolicyParagraph: If this policy changes meaningfully, we'll update the date at the top of this page. Continued use of Scholar after a change means you accept the updated policy.
settings-rest.chronicUnderestimationSignalHint: A subject consistently takes longer than planned
settings-rest.codeWorksOnceNote: Works once. After they use it, the code stops working.
settings-rest.confirmResetMemoryMessage: Delete everything Scholar has learned? Estimates go back to raw values.
settings-rest.contactParagraph: Questions about privacy or data handling? Email {email}.
settings-rest.customColorHint: Any hue — drag to preview, it saves automatically.
settings-rest.dataNeverLeavesDeviceNote: This data never leaves your device.
settings-rest.dataStorageSecurityParagraph: Your data is stored in a managed Postgres database and encrypted in transit (HTTPS) everywhere. Sensitive tokens (like calendar sync credentials) are additionally encrypted at rest. Only you can see your own homework data through your authenticated account.
settings-rest.deleteAccountDescription: Permanently removes your homework, history, groups you own, and every share you've created. This cannot be undone and there is no backup.
settings-rest.deleteIndividualTasksBulletText: any time from your dashboard — this removes them immediately and permanently.
settings-rest.deleteWholeAccountBulletText: by emailing {email} from the address on your account, with the subject "Delete my Scholar account". We'll permanently delete your account, homework data, and any stored sign-in or calendar-sync tokens within 30 days, and confirm by email once it's done.
settings-rest.deletingYourDataIntro: You're always in control of your data. To delete it:
settings-rest.disconnectCalendarBulletText: from Settings → Calendar, which also revokes Scholar's access token with Google.
settings-rest.examApproachingSignalHint: An exam is close and nothing is scheduled for it
settings-rest.exportEverythingDescription: All your homework, history, subjects and settings as a JSON file. Encrypted API keys and attachment contents are left out on purpose.
settings-rest.homeworkDataBulletText: the tasks, deadlines, subjects, and notes you add — typed, spoken, imported from a Canvas/LMS calendar feed, or synced from Google Calendar if you connect it.
settings-rest.howWeUseItParagraph: Solely to run Scholar for you: showing your tasks, sending reminders, generating AI summaries of your own workload, and — if you turn it on — keeping your tasks in sync with Google Calendar. We do not sell your data, share it with advertisers, or use it to train third-party AI models beyond the request needed to answer your own question inside the app.
settings-rest.languageDescription: These are separate on purpose. You can read an English interface, type in a mix of languages, and still get answers back in whichever you prefer.
settings-rest.mixedInputExampleNote: Mixed input works without changing anything — "physics ka ch 4 friday ko submit karna hai" is read as a Physics assignment due Friday.
settings-rest.notEnoughTimeSignalHint: A task needs more time than remains before its deadline
settings-rest.nothingDueTwoWeeksMessage: Nothing due in the next two weeks.
settings-rest.nothingLearnedYetMessage: Nothing learned yet. Finish a task with the focus timer and it'll start calibrating your estimates.
settings-rest.notificationsDefaultDescription: Allow notifications to see alerts outside the tab.
settings-rest.notificationsDeniedDescription: Blocked in your browser's site settings.
settings-rest.notificationsGrantedDescription: Alerts appear as system notifications while Scholar is running.
settings-rest.notificationsOnToastBody: Scholar will tell you when work is at risk.
settings-rest.overduePileupSignalHint: Three or more tasks are past their deadline
settings-rest.overloadedDaysSignalHint: Several deadlines land on the same day
settings-rest.privacyIntroParagraph: Varaxis Scholar ("Scholar", "we", "us") is a homework organiser built by Varaxis. This page explains what information we collect, why, and how you can control or delete it. It applies to the Scholar web app at scholar-varaxis.vercel.app and to sign-in via Google or GitHub.
settings-rest.privacyPolicyMetaDescription: How Varaxis Scholar collects, uses, and lets you delete your data.
settings-rest.repeatedLatenessSignalHint: A recent pattern of missing deadlines
settings-rest.shareNoLongerAvailableError: That share is no longer available.
settings-rest.shareWithParentDescription: You choose exactly what they can see, and you can stop it at any time. They never get access to your account — only to the summary you pick.
settings-rest.shareWithParentHeading: Share with a parent or guardian
settings-rest.sharedWithYouDescription: Summaries other people have chosen to share. They can stop at any time.
settings-rest.signInMethodsDescription: What you can use to get into this account. Signing in linked more than one automatically when the same email address matched.
settings-rest.signInToLinkHint: Sign out, then sign in with {provider} using this email to link it
settings-rest.studyHoursExplanation: Work isn't scheduled outside this window, so a deadline at 9am tomorrow counts tonight's hours — not the hours you'd be asleep.
settings-rest.studyTimeDescription: Scholar uses this to judge whether you actually have time for a task before it's due — not just how close the deadline is.
settings-rest.summaryOnlyDisclaimer: This is a summary only. Task details, notes, attachments and coach conversations are never shared, and {subjectName} can stop sharing at any time.
settings-rest.testNotificationBody: This is what an alert looks like.
settings-rest.thirdPartySignInParagraph: When you sign in with Google or GitHub, that provider shares only your name, email address, and profile picture with us — enough to create your Scholar account. We never receive your password for that provider, and we never post on your behalf. You can review or remove connected sign-in methods any time from Settings → Account.
settings-rest.usageDataBulletText: basic technical logs (timestamps, error reports) used only to keep the app working and to debug issues.
settings-rest.varaxisIdDescription: One account for Varaxis products. Scholar is the first — others will sign in with this same identity rather than asking you to start again.
settings-rest.whatScholarLearnedDescription: Built only from tasks you finished using the focus timer. Estimates are adjusted toward how long your work actually takes.
settings-rest.yourDataDescription: Everything Scholar holds lives in a database file on this machine. Nothing is sent anywhere except the AI provider you configured, and only when you ask it to read something.

teach.gradebookWeightsIncomplete: Category weights do not add up to 100%. Grades are worked out over the weights that exist, so they will change when the rest are set.

timetable.pastePlaceholder:
Paste your timetable however it comes — a grid copied from a PDF, a list, whatever your school gives you. For example:

Mon  P1 08:40 Maths R12   P2 09:40 Physics Lab2
Tue  P1 08:40 English R4  P2 09:40 Chemistry R9
...
timetable.setupTabDescription: Import or fix your timetable here any time — the same list is used everywhere in Scholar, including Settings → Preferences. Breaks and library periods can be imported too — tag them from the timetable text or fix the tag afterwards below.
